agree.reason: The two traffic-focused commissioners get a concrete fix they can vote for, the signal as a binding condition that keeps Alder and 4th at a C rating, though opposed neighbours will probably stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the facts the writer had, the speaker states her church membership up front and refuses to promise traffic won't get worse, and the only small stretch is calling 64/412 'about one in six' (it is closer to one in 6.4).

works_the_facts.reason: Turning 64 units into a share of the 412-household waiting list is a strong, true derivation, but the speech leaves other figures unused, such as the parking ratio of 1.1 spaces per unit or the fact that the 3-year wait grows longer with no new supply.

right_comparison.reason: The no-build alternative is described accurately (an empty lot, 412 households still waiting, and traffic that already backs up), but the speech doesn't say whether the waiting list or the shortage is getting worse.

qualification.reason: The signal condition is specific and checkable against the traffic study's C-versus-D ratings, but it has no deadline, such as requiring the signal to be in place before occupancy, and no consequence if it isn't built.

objections.reason: Traffic, parking and 20 months of construction are each met directly with something the facts support (the signal, weekday parking in writing, and the speaker's own seat on the neighbour group), and no objection is raised that the facts already answer.

fit.reason: At about 400 words it is a spoken public comment that fits the 3-minute limit, with the request stated at the start and again at the end.
